item.title: New requirements for SNAP benefits go into effect Sunday. What does this mean for SNAP benefit recipients?
item.description: New requirements for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits go into effect Sunday, Feb. 1, and those who have not met those requirements could lose their benefits soon.

item.title: Suspect taken into custody following hours-long SWAT incident in South Shore, Chicago police say
item.description: Chicago police say officers were on scene at an active SWAT incident that lasted for hours on Sunday in the South Shore neighborhood.

item.title: Lanes open again after 6-vehicle crash on NB Edens Expressway early Sunday morning, police say pedestrian also hit in crash
item.description: A six-vehicle crash in the north suburbs that also involved a pedestrian being get closed multiple lanes on the northbound Edens Expressway near Dempster Street for several hours early Sunday morning.

item.title: White Sox acquire Hicks, prospect, 2 PTBNL in trade with Red Sox
item.description: CHICAGO (WGN) — The Chicago White Sox are bringing in another pitching reclamation project after a trade with their counterparts from Boston. The White Sox have acquired right-handed pitcher Jordan Hicks, minor league right-hander David Sandlin, cash considerations and two players to be named later (PTBNL) from the Boston Red Sox. item.title: Man charged with killing pregnant woman in Downers Grove released from hospital, back in custody, DuPage County authorities say
item.description: The Westmont man charged with killing a pregnant woman in Downers Grove last week has been released from the hospital after being treated for apparently self-inflicted injuries and is back in custody at the DuPage County Correctional Facility, the DuPage County Sheriff's Office said in a news release Sunday.

item.title: Stair climbers 'Step Up for Kids' at the Aon Center to help support Lurie Children's Hospital
item.description: Over 1,700 people climbed 1,643 steps at the Aon Center to raise $700,000 for critical care programs at Lurie Children's Hospital as part of the "Aon Step Up for Kids" event.

item.title: Johnson says no quick House vote to end partial shutdown
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson said Sunday it will be a few days before a government funding package comes up for a vote, all but ensuring the partial federal shutdown will drag into the week.

item.title: Monday forecast: Spotty snow overnight, mostly sunny by afternoon
item.description: Clouds will continue to move in late Sunday night, bringing light snowfall into the early morning hours Monday. Some areas could see slick spots, but most locations are expected to pick up only a light coating. Totals will only be around a half inch of snow.

item.title: Dixmoor residents left without water after sixth water main break in a week
item.description: A major water main break in Dixmoor, Illinois is impacting over half of the village, with 800-1,000 homes affected, due to aging infrastructure and freezing temperatures.

item.title: Frustrated NIPSCO customers rally in Northwest Indiana over skyrocketing energy bills
item.description: With winter still in full swing, frustration is boiling over in Northwest Indiana. Dozens of NIPSCO customers lined the sidewalk along 167th Street outside the company’s Hammond office Sunday afternoon, demanding answers as their gas and electric bills continue to climb.
